document_name: A Brief History of Artificial Intelligence (demo)
description: A pre-extracted knowledge graph tracing computing from Babbage's Analytical Engine to modern GraphRAG. Loaded by `python -m scripts.seed_demo` so a fresh clone shows a real graph without any AI provider key.

entities.name: Ada Lovelace
entities.description: English mathematician who published the first algorithm intended for a machine, in 1843.

entities.name: Charles Babbage
entities.description: Victorian mathematician who designed the Difference and Analytical Engines.

entities.name: Alan Turing
entities.description: British mathematician who formalised computation and founded modern computer science.

entities.name: John von Neumann
entities.description: Hungarian-American polymath who defined the stored-program computer architecture.

entities.name: Claude Shannon
entities.description: American engineer who founded information theory and digital circuit design.

entities.name: John McCarthy
entities.description: Computer scientist who coined the term artificial intelligence and created Lisp.

entities.name: Frank Rosenblatt
entities.description: Psychologist who built the Perceptron, the first trainable neural network machine.

entities.name: Geoffrey Hinton
entities.description: Cognitive scientist known as a godfather of deep learning; Turing Award 2018.

entities.name: Yann LeCun
entities.description: French computer scientist who developed convolutional neural networks.

entities.name: Yoshua Bengio
entities.description: Canadian researcher whose lab advanced deep learning and neural attention.

entities.name: Fei-Fei Li
entities.description: Stanford professor who created ImageNet and co-directs the Stanford HAI institute.

entities.name: Ashish Vaswani
entities.description: Lead author of the 2017 paper that introduced the Transformer architecture.

entities.name: Ilya Sutskever
entities.description: Deep learning researcher, AlexNet co-author and OpenAI co-founder.

entities.name: Demis Hassabis
entities.description: Neuroscientist and chess prodigy who co-founded DeepMind in London.

entities.name: Turing Machine
entities.description: Abstract model of computation defining what any algorithm can compute.

entities.name: Turing Test
entities.description: Imitation game proposed in 1950 to judge machine intelligence by conversation.

entities.name: Artificial Intelligence
entities.description: Field devoted to building machines that perform tasks requiring human intelligence.

entities.name: Information Theory
entities.description: Mathematical theory of entropy, compression and reliable communication.

entities.name: Perceptron
entities.description: Single-layer learning algorithm for binary classification, introduced in 1958.

entities.name: Neural Network
entities.description: Layered network of weighted units that learns representations from data.

entities.name: Backpropagation
entities.description: Gradient algorithm that assigns error credit through a network's layers.

entities.name: Deep Learning
entities.description: Machine learning with many-layered neural networks trained on large datasets.

entities.name: Convolutional Neural Network
entities.description: Network using shared convolution filters, dominant in computer vision.

entities.name: Attention Mechanism
entities.description: Lets a model weight the most relevant parts of its input dynamically.

entities.name: Transformer
entities.description: Attention-only architecture that parallelises sequence modelling.

entities.name: Large Language Model
entities.description: Transformer trained on internet-scale text to predict and generate language.

entities.name: Hallucination
entities.description: Fluent but factually wrong model output, the core reliability problem of LLMs.

entities.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entities.description: Grounding a language model on documents fetched at query time.

entities.name: Knowledge Graph
entities.description: Graph of typed entities and relationships that machines can traverse and reason over.

entities.name: Vector Embedding
entities.description: Dense numeric vector placing similar meanings close together in space.

entities.name: Analytical Engine
entities.description: Babbage's never-completed mechanical general-purpose computer, designed from 1837.

entities.name: ENIAC
entities.description: 1945 US machine, the first programmable general-purpose electronic computer.

entities.name: ImageNet
entities.description: Dataset of 14 million labelled images that made large-scale vision benchmarking possible.

entities.name: AlexNet
entities.description: 2012 GPU-trained network that crushed the ImageNet benchmark and launched the deep learning boom.

entities.name: AlphaGo
entities.description: DeepMind system that defeated world champion Lee Sedol at Go in 2016.

entities.name: Attention Is All You Need
entities.description: 2017 paper introducing the Transformer, now the most cited work in modern AI.

entities.name: GPT-3
entities.description: 175-billion-parameter model that demonstrated few-shot learning at scale in 2020.

entities.name: Synapse
entities.description: GraphRAG explorer that turns documents into a queryable Neo4j knowledge graph.

entities.name: NVIDIA
entities.description: Chip designer whose GPUs became the default hardware for training neural networks.

entities.name: OpenAI
entities.description: San Francisco lab behind the GPT model family and ChatGPT.

entities.name: Anthropic
entities.description: AI safety company founded in 2021, developer of the Claude model family.

entities.name: Google DeepMind
entities.description: London-founded lab behind AlphaGo, AlphaFold and the Gemini models.

entities.name: Google Brain
entities.description: Google research team that produced TensorFlow and the Transformer paper.

entities.name: Meta AI
entities.description: Meta's research division, home of PyTorch and the Llama open-weight models.

entities.name: University of Cambridge
entities.description: English university where Turing studied and Babbage held the Lucasian chair.

entities.name: University of Toronto
entities.description: Canadian university whose lab produced backpropagation research and AlexNet.

entities.name: Dartmouth Workshop
entities.description: 1956 summer project that named artificial intelligence and founded the field.

entities.name: AI Winter
entities.description: Periods in the 1970s and late 1980s when AI funding and interest collapsed.

entities.name: Bletchley Park
entities.description: Wartime British codebreaking site where Turing helped break the Enigma cipher.

entities.name: GPU
entities.description: Massively parallel processor whose matrix throughput makes deep learning practical.

entities.name: CUDA
entities.description: NVIDIA's parallel computing platform that opened GPUs to general-purpose code.

entities.name: PyTorch
entities.description: Define-by-run deep learning framework that became the research standard.

entities.name: Neo4j
entities.description: Native graph database with Cypher queries, full-text and vector indexes.
